findings.mechanism: ChargeService.charge() (ChargeService.java:70) puts every ticket into the static ConcurrentHashMap AWAITING, keyed by ticket id. The only removal is InFlightCharges.complete(), and ChargeListener calls it only in onPosted (ChargeListener.java:20). onRejected (line 25) and onExpired (line 30) notify the customer but never call complete(), so declined and expired charges stay in the map for the life of the JVM. Each entry retains a PendingCharge and its ChargeRequest, which holds the account id, invoice number, currency and customer email strings. The map is also never bounded or swept.
findings.cause: missing cleanup on the rejected and expired callback paths. A fix is to call InFlightCharges.complete(ticket.id()) in onRejected and onExpired, or in a finally/common terminal path. Expiring stale entries would also work.
findings.evidence: Static code reading only. I could not run it: the internal ledger-client 3.2.1 jar is not in the local Maven repo (only a .lastUpdated marker), and the Maven plugins are not cached offline, so mvn test and the Main load driver would not build. The growth was therefore not measured. The in-flight count that Main prints (service.inFlight()) after ledger.drain() should stay above zero by the number of declined plus expired charges.
findings.discriminator: After drain(), AWAITING.size() should equal the declined plus delayed counters in CustomerNotifier.summary(). If it is zero, the leak is ruled out.
